value.body: A network engineer sets up, configures and maintains the networks that link an organisation's computers, servers and offices. IT services firms, telecom operators, data centres, banks and large companies hire them. A day involves monitoring the network, configuring routers and switches, fixing outages and handling tickets.

items.label: Common certifications
items.value: CCNA, CompTIA Network+, cloud networking certificates

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Shift-based network operations centre (NOC) roles are common at entry

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start in network support or NOC roles at IT services or telecom firms. A vendor-neutral or vendor certification such as CCNA, plus lab practice, is a common way to get shortlisted.

value.title: At a glance
items: Early roles often involve night or rotational shifts.
Common next roles: senior network engineer, network security engineer, cloud network engineer.
Cloud networking skills are increasingly asked for alongside on-site networks.
